title: calotropis procera subsp. hamiltonii
intro: Calotropis procera subsp. hamiltonii, commonly known as the Crown Flower or Giant Milkweed, is a plant species that belongs to the Apocynaceae family. This plant has been found to have various health benefits, including its use in traditional medicine to treat conditions such as fever, rheumatism, and skin infections, due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Calotropis procera subsp. hamiltonii include its ability to act as an analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory, making it a potential treatment for pain and fever reduction. The bioactive constituents responsible for its therapeutic actions include alkaloids, glycosides, and flavonoids, which have been identified in various studies to have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.
